images.seen: Start anchor: Egypt on the Nile, Sumerian city-states/Kish/Mari/Ebla, Anau, Ahar-Banas and the Indus Valley Civilisation as five large blobs over Sindh/Punjab/Cholistan/Haryana (343-378 cells) against only three tiny Cliopatria blobs; nothing misplaced otherwise.

Elam now holds Khuzestan plus Ilam (elam_-2700 keyframe, Cliopatria has no Elam shape), Sumerian city-states and Kish redrawn west of it; the Indus Valley Civilisation drops to the dossier keyframe (about 130 cells in five small blobs near Mehrgarh, Harappa and the Ghaggar-Hakra), so the Cholistan/Punjab/Haryana/Rajasthan land goes unclaimed. Nothing else wrong.

Old Kingdom of Egypt on the Nile, Yamnaya, Anau, Elam, Hoabinhian, Longshan/Dawenkou/Qujialing/Majiayao/Liangzhu, Jeulmun and Jomon all in plausible places and unchanged in outline since -2700; no holes, no stray cells beyond one 1-cell Anau speck.

issues.what: Keyframe snap at -2700: indus-valley-civilization is cut from 378 to 130 cells (248 removed: Punjab (Pakistan) 154, Rajasthan 39, Haryana 33, +1 more) with no ledger event. Origin is outside this window: hakra-ware-culture/ledger/1 (dissolve at -3000, successor indus-valley-civilization) hands 251 Hakra-Ware cells (Bahawalpur, Sirsa, Faisalabad area minus Harappa) to the Indus dossier by succession in -3000 (draft m3000-m2901, change 'hakra-ware-culture/ledger/1' n=251), but the Indus dossier's own keyframes (-3000: 92 cells; -2700: 130 cells, 'Cliopatria -2700 shape + Harappa 60 km + Mehrgarh 50 km') never claim that land, so the snap drops it at -2700 (its note says 'Only the years move', i.e. it was meant to start at -2800, but it has no from). The Hakra page calls Hakra Ware 'contemporaneous with the early Harappan Ravi phase culture (3300-2800 BCE)' and says Kot Diji follows it, but gives no date or place for the land leaving or staying in the Early Harappan culture, so no sourced event or override can be written for -2700.
Size-rule conflict elam / sumerian-city-states, 1 cell (Ilam), smaller state (Sumerian city-states) won.

Elam gains 316 cells at -2700 (elam/ledger/1: Khuzestan + Ilam, Old Elamite period 'c. 2700 - c. 1500 BC', keyframe elam_-2700 in the dossier) and Sumerian city-states gain 74 (ledger/4, Early Dynastic II-III); both are dated ledger events with the dossier's own source and match the images.
Old Kingdom of Egypt takes over the 319 cells of the Early Dynastic Period at -2686 (Djoser, Third Dynasty); same outline, an ordinary succession.

anau-culture owns one detached cell at about 37.4 N 54.5 E (the Turkmen coast left over where the keyframe minus Iran cuts the Bojnurd/Shahrud discs), 198 cells in the main body. One cell; not worth a keyframe override that would span -4500 to -1100, far outside this window.

dossier_requests.what: Make the dossier consistent with its predecessor handoff: either keep the Hakra-Ware land (Bahawalpur, Sirsa, Faisalabad area) in the keyframes -3000 and -2700 (and give indus-valley-civilization_-2700 the 'from' -2800 that its note intends), or drop the Hakra-Ware successor handoff to the Indus state in hakra-ware-culture, so the Indus state does not hold 251 extra cells -3000..-2701 and lose 248 of them at -2700 by a snap.
dossier_requests.why: The -3000 succession gives 343-378 cells, the Indus keyframes 92 and 130; the snap at -2700 is the only place the two meet, and nothing sourced dates the land leaving. The Hakra page says Hakra Ware is 'contemporaneous with the early Harappan Ravi phase culture (3300-2800 BCE)' and that Kot Diji follows it, without placing any change of extent.

problems: indus-valley-civilization: the 248-cell snap at -2700 is a symptom of hakra-ware-culture/ledger/1 (-3000, window m3000-m2901) handing 251 cells to the Indus state by succession while the Indus keyframes never claim them. The next window m2600-m2501 starts from the 130-cell end anchor, so the seam is clean. Left unpatched here because the pages are silent; see dossier_requests.
The Jan-1 -2700 render (start anchor) shows the Indus state much larger than the end of -2700 for the same reason; no neighbour-window patch was written.
